VIC REYNOLDS.name: Vic Reynolds
VIC REYNOLDS.background: Marietta resident. B.S. in criminal justice, Georgia Southern University; law degree, Georgia State University College of Law. Former police officer; partner at the law firm Berry and Reynolds; Cobb County chief magistrate judge; elected Cobb County district attorney twice (re-elected unopposed in 2016); appointed director of the Georgia Bureau of Investigation on Feb. 18, 2019, leading an agency of more than 950 employees; appointed by Gov. Sworn in by Kemp at a private Capitol ceremony, where he pledged, 'I'm going to be fair, I'm going to be punctual.' Kell's unexpired term ran through 2024; Reynolds ran unopposed for the seat in the May 21, 2024 nonpartisan election (68,601 votes).

WILL BOWMAN.name: Will Bowman
WILL BOWMAN.background: Retired U.S. Army drill sergeant; Georgia State Patrol trooper Aug. 2005-Feb. 2016 and Dec. 2016-2019, named Trooper of the Year in 2015 and 2018; elected Liberty County sheriff in 2020 as the county's first African-American sheriff [1][4].
WILL BOWMAN.record: Lost a 2016 Democratic primary challenge to Sheriff Steve Sikes and unsuccessfully challenged the results in court; beat Sikes in the 2020 primary [4]. As sheriff he drew criticism for spending school-zone speed-camera revenue on school and youth groups, including a $20,000 check for a Bradwell Institute band trip; the county commission took control of the account and must approve future spending [1][4]. After deputies stopped and searched a Delaware State University women's lacrosse team bus on I-95, the university's federal civil rights suit led to a consent decree, and the U.S. Justice Department required the office to review its bias-free policing policies [1]. Won the May 21, 2024 Democratic primary without a runoff against four opponents [3]; re-elected Nov. 5, 2024 with 62.7% over Republican Gary Eason [2][3][6]; sworn in for another term [5].
